evidence_sources.rationale: spells/invoke/plan.md is the current Plan mode contract for the subject, required planning parts, gates, execution handoff, evidence ceiling, and non-mutation boundary.
spells/invoke/README.md establishes Invoke ownership, downstream lifecycle consumers, capability-state separation, and Plan handoff limits.
spells/invoke/PLAN-ARTIFACT-BOUNDARIES.md declares the distinct ownership and containment relationships among Implementation Layering, Work Pack, waves, tasks, SWUs, and Execution Pack.
The retired implementation-plan template preserves delivery-slice, task-detail, SWU, validation, blocker, layering, and execution-pack concepts, but WORK-PACK.md now owns the executable plan.
The implementation-layering template defines the global decision-first L0-L3 governance model, evidence-based promotion, deferral, and non-regression conditions.
The Work Pack template materializes the canonical executable hierarchy, validation and stop invariants, execution policy, frontier, entry, and closeout synchronization boundary.
The Execution Pack template confirms the choreography-only role of waves, layer alignment, stage coverage, dependencies, and closure obligations.

The completed historical Plan package demonstrates layers, slices, waves, tasks, SWUs, atomicity, validation, blockers, gaps, ordering, recomposition, and owner handoff; its completion, executable, and authority claims are not current.
DEFINE-SEMANTIC-CONTEXT-3.json preserves the earlier authoring-source, candidate-bundle, admission, and evidence-state concepts but does not cover Plan's internal executable model.
DEFINE-SEMANTIC-CLOSURE-RECEIPT-3.json is historical disposition evidence for the thin model, not current semantic or executable authority.
DEFINE-SOURCE-4.json preserves the separation of authored source, generated candidate, independent admission, and later readiness states while omitting most internal Plan concepts.
bundle/DEFINITIONS.json is historical candidate-definition evidence; its four evidence-layer concepts are reassessed without accepting candidate or authority claims.
DEFINE-BUNDLE-ADMISSION-RECEIPT.json preserves independent replay and claim-ceiling distinctions, but its PASS and authority claims are historical.
DEFINE-SEMANTIC-CONTEXT-6.json expands into Plan, Work Pack, slice, layer, wave, task, SWU, validation, stop, handoff, and choreography concepts; each is reassessed against the newer contract.
DEFINE-SEMANTIC-CLOSURE-RECEIPT-6.json records historical dispositions for the expanded model but is not a correctness or authority oracle.

DEFINE-SOURCE-5.json preserves useful internal Plan relations and boundaries while requiring correction for current closeout, frontier, readiness, atomicity, navigation, and upstream-authority requirements.

facets.rationale: Invoke Plan is the governed, non-executing translation of approved Design outputs into ordered, validated implementation work; its evidence-bearing source and candidate states remain distinct from the Plan itself.

The retained parts are Delivery Boundary, Implementation Layering and its layers, Work Pack, delivery slices, waves, tasks, SWUs, implementation-detail specs, validation contracts, Execution Pack, execution frontier, execution policy, and closeout contract.

The model preserves the admitted-Design dependency, Plan-to-Work-Pack and Plan-to-layering structure, Work-Pack-to-slice/wave/task hierarchy, exactly-one-task ownership of each SWU, layer-aligned wave ordering, validation dependencies, and handoff dependency chain.

Plan authoring source, candidate bundle, independent bundle admission, and Plan evidence state represent authoring and admission without collapsing artifact authorship, readiness proof, owner acceptance, registry release, or execution authority.

Validation strategy, typed validation contracts, Plan gates, blockers, gaps, smallest-coherent-unit selection, SWU atomicity, first-unit narrowness, recomposition, navigation, and layer promotion remain independently testable pass-or-stop obligations.

The handoff layer separately represents the ordered execution frontier, allowed execution policy, per-SWU closeout synchronization contract, exact Execution Entry, and owner-facing execution handoff; none performs implementation.

Approved Design is an externally owned upstream semantic input. Invoke owns Plan authoring only; downstream validators and lifecycle owners retain readiness, acceptance, execution, mutation, promotion, publication, and deployment decisions.

includes: Translation of an approved Design into bounded implementation objective, decomposition, ordering, validation, stop conditions, and handoff.
excludes: Design revision, implementation work, source mutation, acceptance, promotion, publication, and deployment.
conditions: Approved Design references and an explicit delivery boundary are bound before planning.

includes: One machine-readable source containing the Plan's meaning-bearing Work Pack, route, validation, effect, and readiness declarations.
excludes: Generated views, derived digests, validator verdicts, owner acceptance, and execution receipts.
conditions: All generated Plan projections must derive from the same validated source bytes without semantic invention.

includes: The complete deterministic Plan artifact inventory and its producer evidence.
excludes: Independent admission, implementation readiness, owner acceptance, task execution, and mutation.
conditions: Every member must derive from one exact Plan execution source and one producer run.

includes: Independent replay, exact inventory comparison, predecessor freshness, structural checks, and declared consumer results.
excludes: Semantic invention, Design revision, implementation readiness, owner acceptance, execution authorization, and mutation.
conditions: The admission check must be independent from candidate production and bind the exact candidate bytes.

includes: Separate current statements for artifact authorship, admission, readiness proof, owner acceptance, and execution authorization.
excludes: A generic PASS or inference from one evidence axis to another.
conditions: Every positive state must bind current evidence issued by the owner of that state.

includes: Explicit included, excluded, constrained, and deferred delivery scope for the Plan.
excludes: Silent expansion or revision of approved Design decisions.
conditions: Tasks, SWUs, layers, and handoffs must remain within this boundary or stop for a new decision.

includes: The global governance lens owning layer decision questions, boundaries, promotion evidence, deferrals, and non-regression policy.
excludes: Task execution detail, task status tracking, and source-of-truth SWU contracts.
conditions: Every Plan has exactly one global Implementation Layering artifact.

includes: One decision question, minimum working unit, included and deferred scope, exit evidence, and promotion decision.
excludes: An unevidenced maturity label or task status.
conditions: The layer must state what becomes known after it and preserve guarantees established by earlier layers.

includes: The evidence-backed decision to advance, narrow, pivot, remediate, or stop after a layer.
excludes: Promotion by preference, lifecycle authority promotion, or silent inclusion of deferred scope.
conditions: Promotion must cite exit evidence from the preceding layer and preserve its proven guarantees.

includes: Objective, delivery slices, task and SWU manifests, validation, blockers, gaps, gates, current state, and navigable execution links.
excludes: Layer philosophy owned by Implementation Layering and duplicated task-local detail owned by split task contracts.
conditions: Split projections must agree with the Work Pack or its gate blocks.

includes: One coherent delivery outcome with dependencies, layer mapping, and validation.
excludes: Execution ordering, task instructions, and SWU atomicity.
conditions: Every delivery slice maps to at least one Plan task and has a validation strategy.

includes: Wave goal, layer question, ordered tasks and SWUs, dependencies, parallelization boundary, entry gate, and exit evidence.
excludes: Detailed algorithms and source-of-truth SWU definitions.
conditions: Wave ordering must not contradict task or SWU dependencies.

includes: One implementation responsibility with objective, mappings, dependencies, write scope, SWUs, done criteria, validation, handoff, and synchronization.
excludes: Global Plan rationale, unrelated task state, and vague outcome-only instructions.
conditions: A split task file must be a useful executable contract rather than a title placeholder.

includes: One primary behavior or decision, exactly one parent task, dependencies, bounded write scope, completion criteria, acceptance evidence, validation, and handoff context.
excludes: Multiple independently verifiable behaviors bundled for convenience.
conditions: The unit must be independently assignable, executable, reviewable, and verifiable.

includes: Concrete purpose, inputs, outputs, state, algorithm or steps, interfaces, data flow, ordered rules, constraints, edge cases, failure modes, and acceptance checks.
excludes: New architecture decisions owned by Design and outcome-only task descriptions.
conditions: Medium and high complexity execution tasks require this detail; missing acceptance-critical detail blocks handoff.

includes: Medium or high complexity wave order, stage coverage, cross-task dependencies, closure obligations, and parallelization boundaries.
excludes: Source-of-truth task details, SWU definitions, and independent execution state.
conditions: Every referenced unit and dependency must agree with the Work Pack graph.

includes: Plan-wide coverage of validation targets, timing, evidence surfaces, failure behavior, and owners.
excludes: Generic aspirations and evidence that cannot exist at its declared phase.
conditions: Every delivery slice must have validation coverage.

includes: One exact target, phase, command or reviewable check, expected result, evidence output, and failure behavior.
excludes: Unrunnable prose and post-produce evidence represented as a pre-execution PASS.
conditions: Its declared phase must match when the required inputs and outputs can exist.

includes: A named target, required current evidence, accepted outcomes, decision, and causal blocker set.
excludes: Implicit approval and generic PASS without typed evidence.
conditions: Advancement or handoff stops whenever an acceptance-critical gate is not satisfied.

includes: A known cause, affected claim or transition, dependencies, owner, and repair route.
excludes: Non-blocking future improvement and unowned vague concern.
conditions: The condition prevents a named current Plan state, selected unit, gate, or handoff from proceeding.

includes: A missing item, non-blocking rationale, owner, repair route, and escalation condition.
excludes: A condition that already prevents acceptance, readiness, or safe execution.
conditions: The current bounded Plan claim must remain valid without the missing item.

includes: The smallest bounded planning or execution unit that remains meaningful and can recompose into the approved delivery.
excludes: Premature decomposition that destroys semantic closure and oversized work that contains independently acceptable children.
conditions: Plan validation must identify this boundary before mutation-capable routing.

includes: One primary behavior, one independently reviewable acceptance boundary, candidate-child analysis, and retained-boundary rationale.
excludes: Task-shaped units combining independently verifiable behaviors, projections, interactions, or regions.
conditions: If a candidate child can pass independently, the SWU must be split before handoff.

includes: Selection of the narrowest reversible trust-building first SWU.
excludes: A task-shaped first unit that combines baseline proof with later responsive, projection, or interaction work.
conditions: The first selected mutation-capable SWU must pass this condition independently of ordinary task order.

includes: Evidence that selected units, tasks, slices, and waves compose back into the approved Design and delivery boundary.
excludes: Similarity by labels, counts, or filenames.
conditions: A failed acceptance-critical recomposition check blocks mutation-capable handoff.

definitions.term: Navigation to the first executable unit

includes: Navigable links from Work Pack state through the selected task to source anchors and the first executable SWU.
excludes: Repository searching as a substitute for an authored execution path.
conditions: Missing navigation needed to execute the selected unit blocks handoff.

includes: Exact allowed internal routes, write and effect scopes, required inputs, expected receipts, automatic decisions, stop decisions, retry limit, and route digest.
excludes: Undeclared routes, destructive or external effects, semantic choice, scope expansion, authority change, promotion, publication, and deployment.
conditions: Automatic decisions are limited to declared internal and reversible behavior; protected or undeclared effects stop.

includes: The complete finite ordered set of unfinished execution units and their dependency-consistent order.
excludes: Unknown units, omitted mutation-capable units, and an open-ended execution stream.
conditions: Every frontier unit must have exactly one declared execution route and typed validation contract.

includes: Terminal source receipt contract, exact synchronization targets, baseline binding, admitted delta classes, lifecycle-owner validation, expected owner receipt, and deterministic successor policy.
excludes: Implementation admission, another SWU, undeclared targets, authority changes, promotion, publication, deployment, and destructive cleanup.
conditions: Every mutation-capable SWU must have this complete contract before source mutation.

includes: Exact selected unit or truthful selection state, dependencies, route, write and effect scope, admission timing, evidence, validation digest, next owner, and stop conditions.
excludes: Task execution, inferred target scope, implicit successor selection, reusable mutation admission, and broader authority.
conditions: The selected unit and current Plan evidence must pass the applicable entry checks before Task Session routing.

includes: Transfer of exact artifact handles, selected-unit context, validation surfaces, expected receipts, and next-owner identity.
excludes: Execution itself, owner acceptance, reusable mutation authority, and a claim that the downstream lifecycle is complete.
conditions: All Plan gates, closeout prerequisites, navigation, and evidence boundaries must be satisfied for the declared handoff type.

includes: Invoke ownership of intent-to-Plan authoring, planning artifacts, bounded gates, and handoff context.
excludes: Revising approved Design without a routed decision, executing tasks, mutating source, accepting changes, granting runtime authority, promotion, publication, and deployment.
conditions: Each downstream lifecycle owner retains its own readiness, acceptance, execution, mutation, and closeout decisions.

probes.term: Navigation to the first executable unit

consumer_topology.no_consumers_evidence: Not applicable: the current Plan and Invoke contracts explicitly identify the enumerated downstream semantic consumers; templates, historical evidence documents, validators as concepts, routes, techniques, and lifecycle statuses were not added as separate consumers.
